text: Tofacitinib functions as a small-molecule Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that competitively binds to the ATP-binding site of JAK enzymes, preferentially inhibiting JAK1 and JAK3 to disrupt downstream cytokine signaling. In Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA), this blockade prevents the phosphorylation of STAT proteins, thereby suppressing the pro-inflammatory signaling pathways (such as those driven by IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, and IL-21) that contribute to synovial inflammation and joint destruction [PMID: 41656985]. While clinical response to tofacitinib in RA is primarily driven by these anti-inflammatory effects, pharmacogenetic studies suggest that individual variability in treatment outcomes may be influenced by genetic polymorphisms within the JAK-STAT pathway [PMID: 42514924]. Furthermore, the drug's selectivity profile—specifically its relative sparing of JAK2—is clinically significant, as it allows for the management of RA without exacerbating conditions driven by JAK2 mutations, such as polycythemia vera [PMID: 41487987].
